facts.fact: Law 143 of 1994, issued on 7 June 1994, gives the Civil Status Organization of the Ministry of Interior the execution of the law and the registration of births and deaths in the event registers, which Article 3 defines as paper or automated records held on computer, with health offices under the health ministry receiving and entering the notifications and sending them weekly to the civil registry sections.
facts.system: Civil status event registers of the Civil Status Organization

facts.fact: Article 18 of Law 143 of 1994 creates a special fund at the Ministry of Interior, fed first by sums the State allots it in the general budget and also by the Organization's fees, grants, loans and fines, to pay for information centres, automated issuing stations, new civil registry sections and units, equipment and running costs.
facts.system: Civil status event registers of the Civil Status Organization

note: The law sets the procedure, not its medium: the health office enters the notification in its births or deaths ledger at once and sends weekly notices to the civil registry section, which registers within three days; registers may be paper or automated. It does not say which offices use which, so no coverage fact is taken.
